title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez Resigns Following Ethics Report Detailing Sexual Misconduct
snippet: Los Angeles Representative Jimmy Gomez announced his resignation after a House Ethics Committee investigation found substantial evidence of sexual misconduct, weeks after he lost his reelection bid.
content:
WASHINGTON — Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) announced Monday that he will resign from Congress effective Dec. 1 after a House investigation uncovered "substantial evidence" that he engaged in sexual misconduct involving a former congressional staffer.

The report by the House Ethics Committee caps a months-long inquiry into allegations that the five-term Los Angeles Democrat made nonconsensual sexual advances toward a female staffer in her mid-20s. According to the committee, Gomez's actions violated House rules and "could constitute" misdemeanor sexual assault under Washington, D.C., statutes. No criminal charges have been filed against him.

Allegations and Ethics Findings

The ethics panel detailed two separate encounters reported by the former staffer. The first occurred in February 2024 at a Washington, D.C., bar, where she alleged Gomez put his hand down her skirt and penetrated her. A second incident in July 2024 took place in Gomez’s Capitol Hill office, where the staffer testified he forcefully attempted to kiss her as she tried to exit.

"Representative Gomez failed in his obligation to behave in a manner that reflects creditably on the House, and his conduct was exacerbated by his failure to appreciate the inherent power imbalance between House Members and House staff," the committee stated in its report.

While acknowledging personal missteps outside his marriage, Gomez pushed back against the report's conclusions and questioned the panel's process. "I recognize the seriousness of the Ethics Committee’s report and as I previously stated I take full responsibility for the personal mistakes I committed outside of my marriage," Gomez said in a statement, while maintaining that his conduct did not violate the law or chamber rules.

Midterm Defeat and Capitol Hill Scrutiny

The findings follow Gomez’s defeat in this month’s midterm elections, where he lost his seat to Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres by nearly 25 percentage points. The misconduct allegations, which surfaced earlier this year, became a central issue in the campaign, bolstering Gonzales-Torres’s platform centered on ethics and accountability.

Following Monday's announcement, Gonzales-Torres criticized Gomez for not stepping down earlier and addressed the environment in the nation's capital. She noted that the allegations "reflect a broader environment of sexual misconduct and toxic working conditions on Capitol Hill" and pledged to coordinate with regional officials to ensure constituents in California's 34th Congressional District experience no disruption in services during the vacancy.

Gomez is the third male member of Congress to resign this year over sexual misconduct allegations, following the departures of former Reps. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) and Tony Gonzales (R-Texas). Legal counsel representing the former staffer praised the committee's findings as an important step toward addressing systemic workplace harassment in public service.
